audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Cassiopeia four stages and Zaahen none, while every paragraph beneath it says Zaahen wins those stages: whys[1] 'At level 2 you spike', whys[2] 'At level 3 you dominate', whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 even out', whys[5] 'On first item you re-take control', whys[6] 'you still out-duel her one-on-one'. The packet levelChart reads Skill/Zaahen/Zaahen/Skill/Skill/Zaahen/Zaahen — the prose exactly.
audit.why: Zaahen wins 52.23% over 494 games against an immobile mage his kit is built to catch. Both layers agree with each other and both disagree with the packet and with their own explanations.
audit.corrected: Five rows flipped as matched full+content pairs: Level 2, Level 3, First item and 2+ items to Zaahen; Levels 4-5 to Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in roughly twenty fields without its duration, and Twin Fang's cadence is never given.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — 20s at rank 3, one of the longest cooldowns in any top lane. That is the whole engage window and it was left unquantified. Twin Fang is a 0.75s cycle, so 'her E ramps' is really a heal every three-quarters of a second.
audit.corrected: 20s and 0.75s written into breakdown.cooldowns; the Twin Fang cadence and heal into report[5].t and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The slow is attributed to the wrong ability, twice. wants.foe[0] says 'Kiting with Q Noxious Blast slow', whys[3] says 'her Q slow', and spikes[0].text says 'before she stacks her Q Noxious Blast slow'. Riot's text for Noxious Blast is poison damage that grants CASSIOPEIA Move Speed — there is no slow on it. The slow and the grounding both live on Miasma (W). Twin Fang's heal is also missing everywhere.
audit.why: This is the same class of error the calibration notes call out on this exact champion. A player waiting out 'the Q slow' before stepping in will step into the ability that actually stops him — Miasma grounds, so his E dash is off both entering and leaving the cloud. And Twin Fang healing her off poisoned targets is why anti-heal decides the extended trade.
audit.corrected: Slow re-attributed to Miasma in wants.foe[0], whys[3] and spikes[0].text; Twin Fang's heal added to mid, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t buys MR and Mercury's Treads but never Grievous Wounds, despite Twin Fang healing on a 0.75s cycle.
audit.why: Against a heal that ticks every 0.75s, anti-heal timing is the extended trade.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in report[5].t and anti-heal in mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: wants.you[1] 'Turning her R into a whiffed cast by approaching off-angle' is correct — Petrifying Gaze stuns enemies facing her and only slows those with their backs turned. Kept and reinforced in mid.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out as her Q slow and E ramp start punishing bad approaches.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out as Miasma's slow and Twin Fang's heal punish bad approaches.

edits.before: Kiting with Q Noxious Blast slow to keep you at Twin Fang range
edits.after: Kiting with Miasma's slow to keep you at Twin Fang range

edits.before: Cassiopeia has no dash and is a slow, immobile mage; if you get on her she's dead. Use E Golden Onslaught to close and Q Darkin Glaive to trade before her E Twin Fang ramps — every gap you close before she stacks her Q Noxious Blast slow is a winning trade.
edits.after: Cassiopeia has no dash and is a slow, immobile mage; if you get on her she's dead. Use E Golden Onslaught to close and Q Darkin Glaive to trade before her E Twin Fang ramps — every gap you close before she drops Miasma to ground you is a winning trade.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are yours: gap-close on her, deny the free-cast poke, and punish the fact she has no escape from your all-in. At 6 evens as Petrifying Gaze threatens to stun your approach, so come off-angle.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are yours: gap-close on her, deny the free-cast poke, and punish the fact she has no escape. Twin Fang heals her every 0.75s, so buy anti-heal. At 6, come off-angle — Petrifying Gaze only stuns you facing it.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia Miasma: matchup-defining — Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cassiopeia Miasma (20s at rank 3): it grounds — no dash in or out of the cloud, so bait it before you close. - Twin Fang (0.75s): it heals her, so anti-heal early. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Cassiopeia's Miasma: Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. When it is down — Combo the cooldown gap.
edits.after: Twin Fang fires every 0.75s and heals her off poisoned targets — Grievous Wounds is what turns the extended trade in lane.

notes: The Noxious-Blast-slow error here is the exact mistake named in the run's calibration notes, and it appeared in three fields. Separately: diff reads 'FAV' at difficulty 8.5/10 and tone #ff5d6c (hard matchup) while the win rate is 52.23% in Zaahen's favour and the corrected chart now gives him four stages.
